prompt: When does a page's `load` function run, relative to the page rendering?
hint: The component never sees a moment without its data.

choices.text: Only in the browser, after hydration
choices.why: A universal load runs on the server first; a server load only on the server.

choices.text: Whenever the component decides it wants the data, by calling a method named `getData()` on itself
choices.why: There is no such call; SvelteKit calls `load` itself.

choices.text: Before the page renders: its result is the `data`
choices.why: Right: the page gets its data before it renders.

choices.text: After: the page renders, then `load` fills `data` in
choices.why: That was the old `{#await}` way, which this lesson replaces.

prompt: Before the change, `curl` of the home page found no `<title>`. Why?
hint: The title is set on the week page.

choices.text: The week page was inside an `{#await}` that never settles on the server, so it never rendered there
choices.why: Right: no data on the server meant the loading branch, with no title.

choices.text: `curl` cannot see a `<svelte:head>` title
choices.why: It can; after the change the same `curl` found it.

choices.text: The server strips the title to save bytes
choices.why: Nothing strips it; it was simply never rendered.

choices.text: A `<title>` only works once JavaScript runs
choices.why: `<svelte:head>` renders on the server too.

prompt: Why use the `fetch` that `load` receives rather than the global `fetch`?
hint: Two reasons, one per place it runs.

choices.text: It is the only `fetch` that a component is allowed to call from inside its script block
choices.why: The global one works in a component; this is about `load`.

choices.text: It takes a relative address on the server, and reuses the HTML response in the browser
choices.why: Right: both problems the global `fetch` would have.

choices.text: It is faster because it is written in Rust
choices.why: Speed is not the point, and it is not Rust.

choices.text: It encrypts the request
choices.why: It does nothing of the sort.

prompt: What a `load` function returns arrives in the component as a prop called `___`.
hint: SvelteKit's own name for it.

prompt: Which file name makes a `load` function run only on the server?
hint: The rename was the whole fix.

choices.text: `+layout.js`, with `export const ssr = true` set at the top of the file
choices.why: That is universal: it runs in both places.

choices.text: `+server.layout.js`
choices.why: Not a name SvelteKit reads.

choices.text: `+layout.node.js`
choices.why: There is no such convention.

choices.text: `+layout.server.js`
choices.why: Right: a name ending in `.server.js` never goes to the browser.

prompt: Putting the file-reading import in `+layout.js` failed. What exactly broke?
hint: A universal load is sent to the browser to run again.

choices.text: SvelteKit refused to ship the `src/lib/server` module to the browser
choices.why: Right: `server_only_import`, before the file read could even fail.

choices.text: The server could not read the file
choices.why: The server was happy; the title proved it rendered.

choices.text: The data in the file was too large to be serialized and written into the HTML of the page
choices.why: Size was not the issue; the import was.

choices.text: `git mv` corrupted the file
choices.why: `git mv` just moves it.

prompt: Why move `planner.json` out of `static`?
hint: Think about what lesson 14 does, and about more than one user.

choices.text: A JSON file is not allowed in `static`
choices.why: Any file is allowed there.

choices.text: Vite refuses to build with data in `static`
choices.why: It does not; the move is a design choice.

choices.text: `static` is served to anyone, and the file is about to be written to and, for more than one user, be a database
choices.why: Right: reading has to move to the server either way.

choices.text: `static` files cannot be read by `node:fs`
choices.why: They can; the reason is exposure and writing, not reading.

prompt: Besides a name ending in `.server.js`, what else keeps a module off the browser?
hint: A particular folder is treated specially.

choices.text: Importing it only from another `+page.js`
choices.why: A `+page.js` is universal, so that would not keep it off the browser.

choices.text: Putting it in `src/lib/server`
choices.why: Right: that folder is the other server-only place.

choices.text: Putting it in `static`
choices.why: `static` is served to everyone; it is the opposite.

choices.text: Adding `// @server` at the top of it
choices.why: There is no such comment; the folder or the name decides.

prompt: On a client-side navigation, where does the browser get a server load's data from?
hint: The section asked for it by hand.

choices.text: From `localStorage`, where the first visit saved it
choices.why: Nothing is saved there; it is fetched fresh when needed.

choices.text: It reruns the server load in the browser
choices.why: A server load never runs in the browser.

choices.text: From a global `fetch` of `/planner.json`
choices.why: That file is gone; the data comes as `__data.json`.

choices.text: From the page's address with `__data.json` on the end
choices.why: Right: that is where SvelteKit serves it.

prompt: A server load returns `{ ...data, courseName: (id) => ... }`. What happens?
hint: The result has to be written down as data.

choices.text: A 500 on every request
choices.why: Right: `load_not_serializable`, naming `data.courseName`.

choices.text: It works, and the browser is handed the function so that any component can call it
choices.why: Code cannot make the trip as data.

choices.text: The function is silently dropped and the rest arrives
choices.why: It fails loudly, on every request.

choices.text: Only the second visit fails
choices.why: It fails on every request, which is the helpful choice.

prompt: Beyond plain JSON, which can a server load's result carry across to the browser? Choose all that apply.
hint: devalue carries more than JSON, but not code.

choices.text: A `Date`
choices.why: Yes: devalue handles it.

choices.text: A `Map` or a `Set`
choices.why: Yes, both.

choices.text: An object referenced twice, kept as one
choices.why: Yes: it arrives referenced twice, not copied.

choices.text: A function
choices.why: No: code cannot be serialized.

choices.text: An instance of your own class
choices.why: No: its methods are code.

prompt: What does `await parent()` return inside a page's `load`?
hint: Not only the nearest layout.

choices.text: The page's own `params`, the parts of the address the route matched
choices.why: `params` is a separate argument.

choices.text: A promise that never settles on the server
choices.why: It settles once the layouts' loads are done.

choices.text: Every layout above, merged
choices.why: Right: all of them, merged into one object.

choices.text: Only the immediate parent layout's data
choices.why: It merges every layout above, not just the nearest.

prompt: The course page's `load` calls `error(404, ...)` for an unknown course. What does the visitor get?
hint: Compare with lesson 12's answer.

choices.text: A redirect straight back to the planner's home page at `/`
choices.why: `error` does not redirect.

choices.text: The error page, that message, and a 404
choices.why: Right, where lesson 12 answered 200.

choices.text: The page, rendering "No such course" with a 200
choices.why: That was lesson 12; the load now answers 404.

choices.text: A blank page
choices.why: The error page renders, not nothing.

prompt: Why is the course page's `load` a universal `+page.js` and not a `+page.server.js`?
hint: Where do the courses come from?

choices.text: It needs nothing the server has that the browser does not: the courses arrive from the layout
choices.why: Right: so it can run in the browser on later navigations.

choices.text: A course page may not read files, which only a server load can
choices.why: It reads no file; it looks up data it already has.

choices.text: Universal loads are always faster
choices.why: Not the reason; it is about needing the server or not.

choices.text: `error()` only works in a `+page.js`
choices.why: It works in both.

prompt: A `load` needs both its own data and the parent's, and neither depends on the other. Put its body in the order that avoids a waterfall.
hint: Start the work that does not wait, first.
items: Start fetching its own data (do not await yet)
trap: Awaiting parent first would make the own fetch wait for no reason.

prompt: A universal `load` opened by a typed address: where does it run?
hint: On the first page it runs in both places.

choices.text: Only on the server
choices.why: That is a server load; a universal one runs in the browser too.

choices.text: Only in the browser
choices.why: The server runs it first to render the HTML.

choices.text: In neither place, until something on the page asks for the data by pressing a button
choices.why: SvelteKit runs it for the page without being asked.

choices.text: On the server, and again in the browser while hydrating
choices.why: Right: both, on a first visit.

prompt: You click a course link from the week. The course page's universal `load` runs where?
hint: Nothing new appeared in the server's terminal.

choices.text: In both, as on a first visit
choices.why: Only the first visit runs it in both.

choices.text: Nowhere, because the data is cached
choices.why: It ran: the console printed its line.

choices.text: Only in the browser
choices.why: Right: a client-side navigation runs the universal load in the browser alone.

choices.text: Only on the server
choices.why: The server was not asked; the browser ran it.

prompt: What is true of a universal `load` because it runs in two places? Choose all that apply.
hint: Think server and browser, and side effects.

choices.text: It cannot use `window`, `localStorage` or `node:fs`
choices.why: Yes: each exists on only one side.

choices.text: A side effect in it may happen twice on a first visit
choices.why: Yes: once on the server, once in the browser.

choices.text: Its result cannot be a function or class instance
choices.why: No: that is the server load's limit; a universal one may return them.

choices.text: Counting or logging belongs in a server load instead
choices.why: Yes: a server load runs once per request.

prompt: The planner's layout `load` reads no `params` and no `url`. How often does it run as you click around the group?
hint: SvelteKit tracks what each load reads.

choices.text: Once, for the first page
choices.why: Right: its data was kept across the navigations.

choices.text: Once per navigation
choices.why: Only loads whose inputs changed rerun.

choices.text: Once per course page
choices.why: That is the page's own load, not the layout's.

choices.text: Never again, once SvelteKit has primed a special cache of the layout's data
choices.why: It ran once, for the first page.

prompt: When a `load` reruns and `data` changes, what happens to the component?
hint: Think about `new Planner(untrack(() => data))`.

choices.text: Nothing: a rerun does not touch the component
choices.why: It does update the `data` prop.

choices.text: It is not recreated; it gets the new `data` as a changed prop
choices.why: Right: which is why a component that read `data` once keeps what it read.

choices.text: It is destroyed and created again with the new data
choices.why: No: SvelteKit keeps it and updates the prop.

choices.text: Its `$state` is reset to the new data
choices.why: Nothing resets it; the prop changes, the state does not follow.

prompt: To rerun every load function of the current page by hand, call `___()` from `$app/navigation`.
hint: Its older name was `invalidateAll`.

prompt: You must read a private API key and query a database for the planner's data. Which load, and why?
hint: What must never reach the browser?

choices.text: A universal load, so it can run in the browser too
choices.why: That would ship the secret to the browser, which SvelteKit refuses.

choices.text: Either; it makes no difference for secrets
choices.why: It makes all the difference: a universal load is public.

choices.text: Neither; fetch the key in the component
choices.why: A component runs in the browser too; same exposure.

choices.text: A server load, so the key never reaches the browser
choices.why: Right: secrets and a database belong on the server only.

prompt: A server load returns the whole data file, including a field no component shows. Is that field safe?
hint: Whatever a server load returns, the visitor can read.

choices.text: Yes, as long as it is a server load
choices.why: A server load's return is exactly what is public.

choices.text: Only if `__data.json` is disabled
choices.why: It is also inlined in the HTML; you cannot hide it.

choices.text: No: the visitor reads it in the HTML or at `__data.json`, shown or not
choices.why: Right: return only what the pages need.

choices.text: Yes: a field no component renders is never sent
choices.why: Everything returned is sent, whether displayed or not.
